🇷🇺 Russia's weekly oil export earnings near their highest since the start of the SMO, Bloomberg reports

In the week to September 27, Russia shipped an average of 3.99 million barrels of crude per day abroad. The estimated value of those cargoes reached $2.75 billion, up $180 million from the previous week.

Prices did most of the work. In mid-September, Urals from Russia's western ports traded above $110 a barrel and ESPO from the Far East topped $120, as damage to a key Saudi pipeline kept Brent high. More crude is also going abroad because Ukrainian drone strikes have hit domestic refining and a diesel export ban is keeping fuel on the home market.

Bloomberg is keen to stress that the diesel ban eats into the windfall. Four years of sanctions meant to choke off Russian oil revenue, and weekly earnings are closing in on wartime highs anyway.
